tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Give helper functions a new Verb-Noun name such as Read-Doc, also in script files. A built-in alias (rd, rm, del, ri, sc, mv and others) runs instead of a function with the same name, with no warning.
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.
    - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, .claude/settings.local.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

- **3D and vision models:** turning plans, photos and site data into 3D buildings and scenes.

- **Datasets and evals for agents:** like CartTrace-100k.

| | |
|---|---|

## 2. The problem

A real estate developer in Bangkok owns a plot. Before paying an architect, they want to know what they can build on it: how big, how tall, and what it might look like.

The answer depends on building regulations that change by zone. In Bangkok these are spread across separate documents, often only in Thai.

You don't need to know architecture or Thai building law going in.

## 3. What to build

A tool. Given a plot and a building type, it shows what's allowed and the concept designs that fit, in 3D.

- **Input:** the plot, its location or zone, the road it faces, and a building type (for example, a condo).
- **Output:** the rules that apply, such as floor area ratio, open space, setbacks and height. The space the building is allowed to fill. At least two designs that fit, each with a pass/fail checklist.
- **Scope:** one zone in Bangkok, done properly.

- **Any plot shape:** the plot is drawn on a map. Real plots are rarely rectangles.
- **Accurate:** the allowed space follows the plot's real outline, each rule visibly changes it, and the floor areas add up.
- **Real site:** the plot sits in 3D among the actual buildings and roads around it, not on an empty grid.
- **Live:** change the plot, the road or the building type, and everything updates at once, with no reload.
- **Finished:** it runs smoothly on a normal laptop, and looks like something you could put in front of a client.

## 4. How we judge

| | |
|---|---|
| **Thinking** | How you think through a domain you've never seen: how deep your research went, and the calls you made where things were unclear. |
| **Working with AI** | How you work with AI from the first session. |

|---|---|---|

| 4 | Transcripts | Links to your AI sessions, from the very first one. Details below. |

| 6 | Your best project | One link to the most complete project you've owned end to end, and a line on which parts were yours. |
| 7 | About you | A short intro and your links. Details below. |

One page of the doc, with these four headings. We read it as closely as we use the tool.

1. **What you understood.**
2. **What you did, and why.**

4. **What's still wrong, and what you'd do next.**

### Part 4: the transcripts

- Two or three raw, unedited transcripts of your first sessions with AI, starting with the one where you connected to our MCP server and started the assignment, through your research and planning. Not a summary, and not your coding sessions. Link each one from the doc.
- A short note above the links: what did the AI miss, and how did you know it was missing? What made you catch it, and how did you research it?

### Part 5: your setup

A few lines each. Name real tools and real numbers.

1. What tools, models and agents do you use day to day, and for what?

5. How do you get up to speed on a codebase or domain you've never seen?

### Part 7: about you

The basics, kept short. We'll get to know you properly in the interview.

- **Who you are:** a few lines on what you've done so far and what you're doing now.
- **Your links:** rÃ©sumÃ©, LinkedIn, GitHub, and a portfolio or personal site if you have one.
- **Projects:** links to anything else you've built that you want us to see.
- **Anything else:** whatever you'd like us to know. Optional.

Call `submit_application` on this server with your details, the doc's link, the same live link and repo link that are in the doc, and your rÃ©sumÃ© link.

input.description: Research Bangkok zoning FAR/OSR
input.prompt:
Web research task (use WebSearch/WebFetch; no file edits). I'm building a Bangkok plot-feasibility tool for one zone. I need SOURCED numbers, each with a URL and the exact clause/section. Never guess; mark anything unverified as UNVERIFIED.

Research:
1. Bangkok Comprehensive Plan (ผังเมืองรวมกรุงเทพมหานคร), Ministerial Regulation B.E. 2556 (2013): the land-use zone list (ย.1–ย.10, พ.1–พ.5, etc.) with FAR (อัตราส่วนพื้นที่อาคารรวมต่อพื้นที่ดิน) and OSR (อัตราส่วนของที่ว่างต่อพื้นที่อาคารรวม) per zone. Give the full table.
2. Road-width conditions in the plan: e.g. buildings of certain use/size (large buildings, condos/ residential buildings, "อาคารชุด") only allowed on plots fronting public roads of at least X m width, per zone. Condo (อาคารอยู่อาศัยรวม / อาคารชุด) permissions in ย.8, ย.9, ย.10, พ.3–พ.5 especially.
3. FAR bonus provisions (e.g. +20% for public open space, affordable housing, green, parking near transit stations) – just list with numbers and clauses.
4. Status of the draft 4th revision (new Bangkok plan, 2024–2026): has it been enacted as of Nov 2026? If unknown say so. Which plan is in force.
5. Which zone is best for a condo demo: something like พ.3 / ย.9 / ย.10 along Sukhumvit, Sathorn, Silom. Give a specific real area/neighbourhood in that zone.
6. Is there an open GIS layer of Bangkok zoning (BMA, cpd.bangkok.go.th, any GeoJSON/WMS)? URL.
Sources to try: Royal Gazette (ratchakitcha.soc.go.th), cpd.bangkok.go.th, Thai law firm articles (Tilleke & Gibbins, Baker McKenzie, Siam Legal, DLA), Colliers/CBRE/Knight Frank Bangkok reports, thailawonline, Thai Wikipedia. Report a compact table plus citations. State confidence for each number.

input.description: Research Thai building rules + site data
input.prompt:
Web research task (use WebSearch/WebFetch; no file edits). For a Bangkok condo plot-feasibility tool I need SOURCED rules, each with URL and exact clause. Never guess; mark unverified items UNVERIFIED and give confidence.

Part A – Thai building rules (Building Control Act B.E. 2522 and its ministerial regulations):
1. Ministerial Regulation No. 55 (B.E. 2543): setbacks from boundaries (e.g. walls with windows within 2 m/3 m of boundary for buildings ≤9 m / >9 m tall), open space as % of plot (e.g. 30% residential, 10% commercial), setback from road/right-of-way by road width (<6 m, 6–10 m, 10–20 m, >20 m), and height limit relative to road width (height at any point ≤ 2× horizontal distance to opposite side of road – clause number?). Setbacks from public waterways.
2. Ministerial Regulation No. 33 (B.E. 2535) and amendments – high-rise buildings (≥23 m) and large/extra-large buildings (≥2,000 / 10,000 m²): required road frontage (e.g. ≥10 m road, 12 m frontage), fire access space around the building (6 m), setback from boundaries for high-rise (e.g. ≥6 m?), distance from road.
3. Parking requirements for condos/residential buildings in Bangkok (Ministerial Regulation No. 7 B.E. 2517 amendments, Bangkok-specific: e.g. 1 space per 120 m² or per unit ≥60 m²).
4. Bangkok Building Control Ordinance (ข้อบัญญัติกรุงเทพมหานคร ควบคุมอาคาร 2544) – any additional setback/height rules.
5. EIA thresholds for condos (≥80 units or ≥4,000 m²).
6. Definition of building height measurement and which areas are exempt from FAR (parking? ) in Bangkok.

Part B – site data for a browser tool:
7. OpenStreetMap coverage of Bangkok buildings: do footprints have height / building:levels tags commonly? Overpass API endpoint and a sample query for buildings + highways (with width/lanes tags) in a bbox. Rate limits/CORS.
8. Alternatives for 3D context: Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles (needs API key), Overture Maps buildings (heights coverage in Bangkok?), OSM Buildings. Free, no-key options usable from a static Vercel site.
9. Free basemap tiles usable without key (OpenFreeMap, MapLibre demo tiles, Carto) and license notes.
Report compact tables plus citations.

## Part A – Thai building rules

**Main sources:**
- **[S1] MR 55 (B.E. 2543), full text** from the Council of State (Krisdika), hosted by yotathai: https://data.yotathai.org/d/zx9hfz.pdf (Royal Gazette vol. 117, part 75 ก, p. 16, 7 Aug 2543). This is the original 2543 wording.
- **[S2] Bangkok Council committee report (2562)** quoting MR 33 as amended by MR 50 (2540), and the Bangkok Building Control Ordinance 2544: https://bmc.go.th/wp-content/uploads/2020/06/48_2562.pdf

### 1. Ministerial Regulation 55 (all HIGH confidence, original 2543 text)

| Rule | Clause | Exact text (Thai, abridged) |
|---|---|---|
| Open space | ข้อ 33 | (1) อาคารอยู่อาศัย และอาคารอยู่อาศัยรวม ต้องมีที่ว่างไม่น้อยกว่า ๓๐ ใน ๑๐๐ ส่วนของพื้นที่ชั้นใดชั้นหนึ่งที่มากที่สุดของอาคาร. (2) commercial and other non-residential buildings: ๑๐ ใน ๑๐๐, but if also used for living, the 30% applies. |
| What counts as open space | ข้อ 1 | "ที่ว่าง" = area with no roof or structure over it. It may be a pool, wastewater tank, refuse point, or **outdoor parking**. It also includes structures **≤ 1.20 m** above ground with nothing covering them. |
| Road setback | ข้อ 41 | Road **< 6 m** wide: set back **≥ 3 m from the road centreline**. For buildings over 2 storeys or over 8 m, row/shop houses, commercial, factory and public buildings: (1) road **< 10 m** → **≥ 6 m from centreline**; (2) road **10–20 m** → **≥ 1/10 of road width from the road boundary**; (3) road **> 20 m** → **≥ 2 m from the road boundary**. |
| Waterways | ข้อ 42 | Waterway **< 10 m** wide → **≥ 3 m** from its boundary; **≥ 10 m** wide → **≥ 6 m**; large water bodies (บึง, lake, sea) → **≥ 12 m**. Bridges, dams, fences, drains, piers, signs and open-air parking are exempt. |
| Height vs road width | **ข้อ 44** | "ความสูงของอาคารไม่ว่าจากจุดหนึ่งจุดใด ต้องไม่เกินสองเท่าของระยะราบ วัดจากจุดนั้นไปตั้งฉากกับแนวเขตด้านตรงข้ามของถนนสาธารณะที่อยู่ใกล้อาคารนั้นที่สุด". Height is measured vertically **from road level or ground level to the highest part of the building** (gable/hip roofs: to the top of the highest wall). |
| Two roads | ข้อ 45 / ข้อ 46 | ข้อ 45: roads on both sides, ≤ 60 m apart, and the building's frontage on the wider road ≤ 60 m → measure the 2× rule to the far side of the **wider** road. ข้O 46: corner plot → use the wider road; frontage along the narrower road ≤ 60 m (≤ 15 m for shophouses). |
| Window/balcony walls to boundary | ข้อ 50 | Building **≤ 9 m** → **≥ 2 m**. Building **> 9 m but < 23 m** → **≥ 3 m**. Closer than that: a solid wall at least 0.50 m from the boundary, or built on the boundary only if ≤ 15 m tall with the neighbour's written consent. |
| Between buildings on the same plot | ข้อ 48 | ≤ 9 m → 4 m apart; 9–23 m → 6 m apart. **This clause was later amended by MR 61**, so check the current text. |

**Caveats:**
- **MEDIUM:** MR 55 was later amended (MR 61 changed ข้อ 48; MR 68 of 2563 is said to touch the rooftop solid wall in ข้อ 50, per sanook.com, unverified). Confirm the consolidated text before relying on these clauses.
- **UNVERIFIED:** ข้อ 50 only covers buildings under 23 m. I could not find a sourced clause that sets a 6 m window-wall setback for buildings of 23 m or more.

### 2. MR 33 (B.E. 2535), amended by MR 50 (2540) – source [S2], HIGH confidence

| Rule | Clause | Text |
|---|---|---|
| High-rise definition | ข้อ 1 | Height **≥ 23.00 m**, measured from ground level to the roof deck (gable/hip roofs: to the top of the highest wall). |
| Extra-large building | ข้อ 1 | Total floor area of **≥ 10,000 m²**, all floors combined or any single floor. |
| Road frontage | ข้อ 2 | Building area ≤ 30,000 m²: at least one plot side **≥ 12 m long** facing a public road with right-of-way **≥ 10 m**, continuously wide until it joins another road ≥ 10 m. Above 30,000 m²: the same, but the road must be **≥ 18 m**. The access strip must be **≥ 12 m wide** all the way to the building and kept clear for fire trucks. |
| Fire access around the building | ข้อ 3 | "ต้องจัดให้มีผิวถนนที่มีผิวการจราจรกว้างไม่น้อยกว่า 6.00 เมตร ที่ปราศจากสิ่งปกคลุมโดยรอบอาคาร" (a fire-truck road at least 6 m wide, uncovered, all around the building). It may lie inside a road-side no-build zone. |
| Road width with planned widening | ข้อ 4 | If a widening line has been declared, measure road width from that line. |
| FAR cap | ข้อ 5 | FAR (floor area ÷ plot area) **≤ 10:1**, counting all buildings on the plot. |

**Notes:**
- The Supreme Administrative Court (อ. 588/2557, Ashton/Aetas, Soi Ruamrudee) held that the road must be ≥ 10 m **as actually used along its whole length**. Encroachments count against the width. Your tool should treat road width as the narrowest point all the way to a qualifying road.
- **Large building** (Bangkok Ordinance ข้อ 5(101), per [S2]): total area > 2,000 m², or ≥ 15 m tall with total area > 1,000 m².
- MR 69 (2564) renamed Chapter 2 of MR 33 (fire safety), per Thansettakij. It does not appear to change ข้อ 2–5 (MEDIUM).

### 3. Parking for condos in Bangkok – MEDIUM-HIGH (academic source, not the regulation text)

Source: Lertpradit & Charnwasununth, Sarasatr 3/2563, p. 643: https://so05.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/sarasatr/article/download/242164/168262/861885

The paper says the rule comes from **MR 7 (2517) together with the Bangkok Building Control Ordinance 2544**. Exact wording:
- (1) "ห้องชุดพักอาศัยที่มีพื้นที่ตั้งแต่ 60 ตารางเมตรขึ้นไปทุกห้อง จะต้องมีที่จอดรถยนต์ 1 คัน" (every unit of 60 m² or more needs one space)
- (2) Large-building method: "1 คันต่อพื้นที่อาคาร 120 ตารางเมตร" (one space per 120 m² of building area)

Source: Sarasatr 3/2567, p. 730: https://so05.tci-thaijo.org/index.php/sarasatr/article/download/272771/183891/1143741

## Part B – Site data for a browser tool

### 7. OpenStreetMap and Overpass

**Tag coverage** — my own live Overpass count on 2026-11-20 for one Sukhumvit/Asok bounding box (13.725,100.545,13.745,100.570). It is a single sample, not a city-wide figure.

| Feature | Count | Share |

| …with `height` | 175 | ~4% |
| Highway ways | 2,667 | – |
| …with `width` | 8 | ~0.3% |
| …with `lanes` | 172 | ~6% |

So you need fallbacks: road width from road class or a user input, and building height from levels × about 3 m. Note the OSM wiki says `height` includes the roof while `building:levels` does not.

**Endpoint and limits:**
- Main endpoint: `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`. The policy is under 10,000 queries/day and under 1 GB/day; on HTTP 429 or 406, wait 30 s. The wiki asks apps to send a User-Agent. Source: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API
- Alternatives without a key: `overpass.private.coffee` and `maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass`.
- **CORS:** I checked a live POST from a foreign origin. It returned `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so it is usable from a static Vercel site. (A bare request with no proper headers returned 406.)

Sample query:
```
[out:json][timeout:60];
(
  way["building"](S,W,N,E);
  way["highway"](S,W,N,E);
);
out tags geom;
```
Read `building:levels`, `height`, `min_height`, `width`, `lanes`, `highway`. POST it as `data=…` (URL-encoded).

### 7. OpenStreetMap and Overpass

**Tag coverage** — my own live Overpass count on 2026-11-20 for one Sukhumvit/Asok bounding box (13.725,100.545,13.745,100.570). It is a single sample, not a city-wide figure.

| Feature | Count | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Building ways | 4,103 | – |
| …with `building:levels` | 1,185 | ~29% |
| …with `height` | 175 | ~4% |
| Highway ways | 2,667 | – |
| …with `width` | 8 | ~0.3% |
| …with `lanes` | 172 | ~6% |

So you need fallbacks: road width from road class or a user input, and building height from levels × about 3 m. Note the OSM wiki says `height` includes the roof while `building:levels` does not.

**Endpoint and limits:**
- Main endpoint: `https://overpass-api.de/api/interpreter`. The policy is under 10,000 queries/day and under 1 GB/day; on HTTP 429 or 406, wait 30 s. The wiki asks apps to send a User-Agent. Source: https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Overpass_API
- Alternatives without a key: `overpass.private.coffee` and `maps.mail.ru/osm/tools/overpass`.
- **CORS:** I checked a live POST from a foreign origin. It returned `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, so it is usable from a static Vercel site. (A bare request with no proper headers returned 406.)

Sample query:
```
[out:json][timeout:60];
(
  way["building"](S,W,N,E);
  way["highway"](S,W,N,E);
);
out tags geom;
```
Read `building:levels`, `height`, `min_height`, `width`, `lanes`, `highway`. POST it as `data=…` (URL-encoded).

| Provider | Key needed? | Terms | Confidence |

| …with `lanes` | 172 | ~6% |

[out:json][timeout:60];
(

  way["highway"](S,W,N,E);
);
out tags geom;

# Plan: Bangkok plot feasibility tool (zone ย.10, condo)

## Context
The clock started Fri 20 Nov 00:52 IST, and the deadline is **Sun 22 Nov 00:52 IST**.

The brief is in BRIEF.md. The tool takes a plot drawn on a map, its zone, the road it faces and a building type. From those it must show:
- the rules that apply
- the allowed space, following the plot's real outline
- at least 2 designs that fit, each with a pass/fail checklist

All of this is in 3D among the real neighbouring buildings and roads, and updates live. The scope is one zone, done properly. They will try to break it.

Research is done (3 agents this session). Key findings:
- **The 2013 Bangkok plan (B.E. 2556) is still in force.** The 4th-revision draft is not enacted; it is expected around late 2027.
- **Zone ย.10 (Sukhumvit, Phrom Phong to Thong Lo):** FAR 8 and OSR 4% (ข้อ 17). The plan sets no condo size or road condition there. A FAR bonus of up to +20% is possible (ข้อ 53).
- **MR 55 (2543):**
  - open space ≥ 30% of the largest floor for residential buildings (ข้อ 33)
  - road setback by road width (ข้อ 41)
  - height at any point ≤ 2× the distance to the far side of the road (ข้อ 44); corner and two-road cases in ข้อ 45/46
  - window walls ≥ 2 m from the boundary for buildings ≤ 9 m, ≥ 3 m for buildings under 23 m (ข้อ 50)
- **MR 33 (amended by MR 50):**
  - high-rise means ≥ 23 m; extra-large means ≥ 10,000 m²
  - needs a public road ≥ 10 m and frontage ≥ 12 m (≥ 18 m road above 30,000 m²) (ข้อ 2)
  - needs a 6 m fire-access road all round the building (ข้อ 3)
  - FAR ≤ 10 (ข้อ 5)
- **Bangkok ordinance 2544, ข้อ 55:** at least 2 m clear all round a building over 15 m.
- **Parking:** the larger of one space per unit ≥ 60 m² and one space per 120 m² (MR 7 plus the Bangkok ordinance, from a secondary source).
- **EIA:** required at ≥ 80 units or ≥ 4,000 m² (medium confidence).
- **Data:**
  - BMA zoning layer (ArcGIS REST, GeoJSON): `cpudgiapp.bangkok.go.th/.../BMAGI_Planing/MapServer/1`
  - Overpass works from a static site (CORS `*`); only about 29% of buildings have levels and almost no roads have a width tag.
  - OpenFreeMap needs no key.

## Approach

### Stack
Keep the starter: Vite, React, TS and `polygon-clipping`. Add MapLibre GL with OpenFreeMap tiles.

All 3D happens inside MapLibre, using `fill-extrusion` with per-feature `base` and `height`:
- neighbouring buildings come from OpenFreeMap's OpenMapTiles building layer (`render_height`), with Overpass as a fallback or extra source
- the allowed space and the designs are stacked floor polygons

**Why:** the plot, the real site and the designs share one coordinate system and one renderer. There is no second scene to keep in sync, and it is smooth on a laptop.

Keep the starter's SVG plan as the 2D drawing, with a level picker driving both the map and the plan. Drop the PDF/DXF loaders, `pdfjs-dist`, `dxf-parser` and r3f/drei/suncalc.

### Allowed space
This is the core work, in pure functions with unit tests.
1. Project lat/lng to local metres (equirectangular about the plot centroid; error well under 0.1% at plot scale).
2. Classify each edge as a road edge or a side/rear edge. The road edge is auto-detected (the edge nearest a selected OSM road), and the user can toggle it per edge.
3. Base setbacks per edge:
   - **Road edge:** the ข้อ 41 setback for the road width (converting the from-centreline cases to from-boundary).
   - **Other edges:** ข้อ 50 (2 m / 3 m) when below 23 m. For a high-rise, the larger of 6 m (MR 33 ข้อ 3 fire access) and 2 m (ordinance ข้อ 55).
   - Reading MR 33 ข้อ 3 as a 6 m clear zone on the side edges is an interpretation. It goes in DECISIONS.md and is shown as "interpretation" in the tool.
4. Height plane (ข้อ 44): for a floor whose top is at height h, the road edge setback = max(base, h/2 − W), where W is the road width. Run `inset()` per distinct setback, so the allowed space steps back as it rises. Cache by setback value.
5. If the road is under 10 m or the frontage is under 12 m, the high-rise threshold applies: cap the height below 23 m and the floor area below 10,000 m².
6. Area caps:
   - floor area ≤ FAR × plot area, with an optional bonus toggle
   - open space (plot minus footprint) ≥ max(OSR × floor area, 30% of the largest floor)
   - these trim the floor count or footprint
7. Each rule gets a layer toggle ("show the effect of X"), so the effect of each rule on the allowed space is visible.

Reuse `inset`, `clip`, `area`, `centroid` and `largest` from `starter/src/lib/geometry.ts`. Extend `largest` to keep all pieces with a minimum area.

### Designs (3)
Each design is a list of floors, each `{polygon, base, top, use}`:
- **A · Tower on podium:** a parking/amenity podium below 23 m filling the allowed space minus open space; a tower floor plate (editable target, default about 1,000 m²) fitted inside the stepped allowed space.
- **B · Low-rise slab, under 23 m:** avoids the high-rise rules, so it always works on narrow sois.
- **C · Twin towers or an L-shape:** two plates with ≥ the required spacing (ข้อ 48).

Fix `fit()`: bisect the scale factor until the target area is reached within 1%, so concave plots don't come up short.

### Checklist per design
Each item shows the value, the limit, the clause, pass/check/fail, and whether it is sourced or an assumption:
- FAR
- OSR
- open space ≥ 30% of the largest floor
- road setback
- side/rear setbacks
- ข้อ 44 height plane
- high-rise road width and frontage
- floor area ≤ 10,000 m² (where it applies)
- parking required vs provided
- EIA flag
- 50% of open space planted

Extend `check()` with a direction (max or min).

### Area statement
Floor-by-floor area table. Gross floor area = sum of the floors. Carpet area is estimated with an editable efficiency (assumption). Unit yield from an editable average unit size (assumption). A test asserts that the sum of the floors equals the total and that FAR = total ÷ plot area.

### Rules data
`src/rules/bangkok.ts`: one typed table where each value has `{value, clause, source URL, status: 'sourced' | 'assumption' | 'interpretation'}`. Zone lookup uses a static `public/zones-y10.geojson` (ย.10/พ.5 polygons around Sukhumvit, pre-fetched from the BMA layer with outSR=4326). If the plot falls outside ย.10, the tool warns that it is scoped to ย.10.

### Live and smooth
- One state object and the URL hash for sharing (starter pattern).
- Calculations are memoised and run on requestAnimationFrame while a corner is dragged.
- The map's GeoJSON sources are updated with `setData`, never rebuilt.
- A preloaded sample plot (a real irregular plot on Sukhumvit Soi 31/33) shows a result in one click.

## Steps (all times IST)
1. **Now:** save the research as `references/BANGKOK.md` (rules table plus citations) and create `DECISIONS.md` (zone choice, 2556 plan not the draft, ย.10, MapLibre-only 3D, the 6 m side-edge reading, height via ข้อ 44). Check CORS on the BMA layer and OpenFreeMap building heights at Phrom Phong.
2. MapLibre map plus plot drawing (click to add corners, drag corners, close the shape) and the sample plot. Deploy to `siliconbricks-assignment.vercel.app`.
3. Projection, edge classification, the allowed-space engine and tests. Show the stepped allowed space in 3D.
4. Rules panel, then 3 designs, checklists and the area statement. Deploy.
5. Context: building extrusions with estimated heights labelled as estimates, a road-width editor, Overpass fallback.
6. Try to break it: self-intersecting shapes (reject with a message), slivers, no road edge, tiny plots, a 4 m soi. Error states.
7. Polish: layout, phone width, load time, README. **First submission by Sat 18:00 IST.**
8. You write the doc; I supply facts and numbers. Transcripts, private-window link checks, final resubmission, `check_submission`.

Remind you to commit after steps 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7. Claude does no git writes.

## Critical files
- Edit:
  - `starter/src/lib/geometry.ts`
  - `starter/src/lib/massing.ts` → `designs.ts`
  - `starter/src/App.tsx`
  - `starter/src/components/PlanView.tsx`
- New:
  - `starter/src/lib/envelope.ts`
  - `starter/src/lib/project.ts`
  - `starter/src/rules/bangkok.ts`
  - `starter/src/components/MapView.tsx`
  - `starter/public/zones-y10.geojson`
- Delete:
  - `starter/src/lib/loaders.ts`
  - `starter/src/components/Viewer.tsx`
  - `starter/src/lib/sun.ts`
- Docs:
  - `references/BANGKOK.md`
  - `DECISIONS.md`
  - `PLAN.md` status

## Verification
- Run `pnpm vitest run`:
  - projection round trip
  - per-edge inset on a concave plot
  - ข้อ 41 table at each road-width band
  - ข้อ 44 step at a known height
  - floor areas sum to the total
  - FAR, OSR and 30% open space at the pass/fail boundaries
- Run `pnpm build` cleanly.
- Playwright on the live URL at 1440×900 and 390×844:
  - draw a plot and drag a corner; the allowed space and checklist update with no reload
  - change the road width from 12 to 8 m; the high-rise checks fail and design B still passes
  - screenshots saved
- `time_left` checked before every submission.
