tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

input.plan:
# Plan: Bangkok plot feasibility tool (zone ย.10, condo)

## Context
The clock started Fri 20 Nov 00:52 IST, and the deadline is **Sun 22 Nov 00:52 IST**.

The brief is in BRIEF.md. The tool takes a plot drawn on a map, its zone, the road it faces and a building type. From those it must show:
- the rules that apply
- the allowed space, following the plot's real outline
- at least 2 designs that fit, each with a pass/fail checklist

All of this is in 3D among the real neighbouring buildings and roads, and updates live. The scope is one zone, done properly. They will try to break it.

Research is done (3 agents this session). Key findings:
- **The 2013 Bangkok plan (B.E. 2556) is still in force.** The 4th-revision draft is not enacted; it is expected around late 2027.
- **Zone ย.10 (Sukhumvit, Phrom Phong to Thong Lo):** FAR 8 and OSR 4% (ข้อ 17). The plan sets no condo size or road condition there. A FAR bonus of up to +20% is possible (ข้อ 53).
- **MR 55 (2543):**
  - open space ≥ 30% of the largest floor for residential buildings (ข้อ 33)
  - road setback by road width (ข้อ 41)
  - height at any point ≤ 2× the distance to the far side of the road (ข้อ 44); corner and two-road cases in ข้อ 45/46
  - window walls ≥ 2 m from the boundary for buildings ≤ 9 m, ≥ 3 m for buildings under 23 m (ข้อ 50)
- **MR 33 (amended by MR 50):**
  - high-rise means ≥ 23 m; extra-large means ≥ 10,000 m²
  - needs a public road ≥ 10 m and frontage ≥ 12 m (≥ 18 m road above 30,000 m²) (ข้อ 2)
  - needs a 6 m fire-access road all round the building (ข้อ 3)
  - FAR ≤ 10 (ข้อ 5)
- **Bangkok ordinance 2544, ข้อ 55:** at least 2 m clear all round a building over 15 m.
- **Parking:** the larger of one space per unit ≥ 60 m² and one space per 120 m² (MR 7 plus the Bangkok ordinance, from a secondary source).
- **EIA:** required at ≥ 80 units or ≥ 4,000 m² (medium confidence).
- **Data:**
  - BMA zoning layer (ArcGIS REST, GeoJSON): `cpudgiapp.bangkok.go.th/.../BMAGI_Planing/MapServer/1`
  - Overpass works from a static site (CORS `*`); only about 29% of buildings have levels and almost no roads have a width tag.
  - OpenFreeMap needs no key.

## Approach

### Stack
Keep the starter: Vite, React, TS and `polygon-clipping`. Add MapLibre GL with OpenFreeMap tiles.

All 3D happens inside MapLibre, using `fill-extrusion` with per-feature `base` and `height`:
- neighbouring buildings come from OpenFreeMap's OpenMapTiles building layer (`render_height`), with Overpass as a fallback or extra source
- the allowed space and the designs are stacked floor polygons

**Why:** the plot, the real site and the designs share one coordinate system and one renderer. There is no second scene to keep in sync, and it is smooth on a laptop.

Keep the starter's SVG plan as the 2D drawing, with a level picker driving both the map and the plan. Drop the PDF/DXF loaders, `pdfjs-dist`, `dxf-parser` and r3f/drei/suncalc.

### Allowed space
This is the core work, in pure functions with unit tests.
1. Project lat/lng to local metres (equirectangular about the plot centroid; error well under 0.1% at plot scale).
2. Classify each edge as a road edge or a side/rear edge. The road edge is auto-detected (the edge nearest a selected OSM road), and the user can toggle it per edge.
3. Base setbacks per edge:
   - **Road edge:** the ข้อ 41 setback for the road width (converting the from-centreline cases to from-boundary).
   - **Other edges:** ข้อ 50 (2 m / 3 m) when below 23 m. For a high-rise, the larger of 6 m (MR 33 ข้อ 3 fire access) and 2 m (ordinance ข้อ 55).
   - Reading MR 33 ข้อ 3 as a 6 m clear zone on the side edges is an interpretation. It goes in DECISIONS.md and is shown as "interpretation" in the tool.
4. Height plane (ข้อ 44): for a floor whose top is at height h, the road edge setback = max(base, h/2 − W), where W is the road width. Run `inset()` per distinct setback, so the allowed space steps back as it rises. Cache by setback value.
5. If the road is under 10 m or the frontage is under 12 m, the high-rise threshold applies: cap the height below 23 m and the floor area below 10,000 m².
6. Area caps:
   - floor area ≤ FAR × plot area, with an optional bonus toggle
   - open space (plot minus footprint) ≥ max(OSR × floor area, 30% of the largest floor)
   - these trim the floor count or footprint
7. Each rule gets a layer toggle ("show the effect of X"), so the effect of each rule on the allowed space is visible.

Reuse `inset`, `clip`, `area`, `centroid` and `largest` from `starter/src/lib/geometry.ts`. Extend `largest` to keep all pieces with a minimum area.

### Designs (3)
Each design is a list of floors, each `{polygon, base, top, use}`:
- **A · Tower on podium:** a parking/amenity podium below 23 m filling the allowed space minus open space; a tower floor plate (editable target, default about 1,000 m²) fitted inside the stepped allowed space.
- **B · Low-rise slab, under 23 m:** avoids the high-rise rules, so it always works on narrow sois.
- **C · Twin towers or an L-shape:** two plates with ≥ the required spacing (ข้อ 48).

Fix `fit()`: bisect the scale factor until the target area is reached within 1%, so concave plots don't come up short.

### Checklist per design
Each item shows the value, the limit, the clause, pass/check/fail, and whether it is sourced or an assumption:
- FAR
- OSR
- open space ≥ 30% of the largest floor
- road setback
- side/rear setbacks
- ข้อ 44 height plane
- high-rise road width and frontage
- floor area ≤ 10,000 m² (where it applies)
- parking required vs provided
- EIA flag
- 50% of open space planted

Extend `check()` with a direction (max or min).

### Area statement
Floor-by-floor area table. Gross floor area = sum of the floors. Carpet area is estimated with an editable efficiency (assumption). Unit yield from an editable average unit size (assumption). A test asserts that the sum of the floors equals the total and that FAR = total ÷ plot area.

### Rules data
`src/rules/bangkok.ts`: one typed table where each value has `{value, clause, source URL, status: 'sourced' | 'assumption' | 'interpretation'}`. Zone lookup uses a static `public/zones-y10.geojson` (ย.10/พ.5 polygons around Sukhumvit, pre-fetched from the BMA layer with outSR=4326). If the plot falls outside ย.10, the tool warns that it is scoped to ย.10.

### Live and smooth
- One state object and the URL hash for sharing (starter pattern).
- Calculations are memoised and run on requestAnimationFrame while a corner is dragged.
- The map's GeoJSON sources are updated with `setData`, never rebuilt.
- A preloaded sample plot (a real irregular plot on Sukhumvit Soi 31/33) shows a result in one click.

## Steps (all times IST)
1. **Now:** save the research as `references/BANGKOK.md` (rules table plus citations) and create `DECISIONS.md` (zone choice, 2556 plan not the draft, ย.10, MapLibre-only 3D, the 6 m side-edge reading, height via ข้อ 44). Check CORS on the BMA layer and OpenFreeMap building heights at Phrom Phong.
2. MapLibre map plus plot drawing (click to add corners, drag corners, close the shape) and the sample plot. Deploy to `siliconbricks-assignment.vercel.app`.
3. Projection, edge classification, the allowed-space engine and tests. Show the stepped allowed space in 3D.
4. Rules panel, then 3 designs, checklists and the area statement. Deploy.
5. Context: building extrusions with estimated heights labelled as estimates, a road-width editor, Overpass fallback.
6. Try to break it: self-intersecting shapes (reject with a message), slivers, no road edge, tiny plots, a 4 m soi. Error states.
7. Polish: layout, phone width, load time, README. **First submission by Sat 18:00 IST.**
8. You write the doc; I supply facts and numbers. Transcripts, private-window link checks, final resubmission, `check_submission`.

Remind you to commit after steps 2, 3, 4, 5 and 7. Claude does no git writes.

## Critical files
- Edit:
  - `starter/src/lib/geometry.ts`
  - `starter/src/lib/massing.ts` → `designs.ts`
  - `starter/src/App.tsx`
  - `starter/src/components/PlanView.tsx`
- New:
  - `starter/src/lib/envelope.ts`
  - `starter/src/lib/project.ts`
  - `starter/src/rules/bangkok.ts`
  - `starter/src/components/MapView.tsx`
  - `starter/public/zones-y10.geojson`
- Delete:
  - `starter/src/lib/loaders.ts`
  - `starter/src/components/Viewer.tsx`
  - `starter/src/lib/sun.ts`
- Docs:
  - `references/BANGKOK.md`
  - `DECISIONS.md`
  - `PLAN.md` status

## Verification
- Run `pnpm vitest run`:
  - projection round trip
  - per-edge inset on a concave plot
  - ข้อ 41 table at each road-width band
  - ข้อ 44 step at a known height
  - floor areas sum to the total
  - FAR, OSR and 30% open space at the pass/fail boundaries
- Run `pnpm build` cleanly.
- Playwright on the live URL at 1440×900 and 390×844:
  - draw a plot and drag a corner; the allowed space and checklist update with no reload
  - change the road width from 12 to 8 m; the high-rise checks fail and design B still passes
  - screenshots saved
- `time_left` checked before every submission.

## Plan in force
- Bangkok Comprehensive Plan, Ministerial Regulation B.E. 2556 (2013), effective 16 May 2013. Still in force (H). The 4th-revision draft finished its 90-day public posting on 9 Nov 2026 and is expected to take effect around late 2027; its zone codes differ from the current ones (for example, draft ย.10 = FAR 5.5, OSR 7.5%). Sources: nationthailand.com/business/property/40073336, thansettakij.com/real-estate/661177
- Official zoning layer: https://cpudgiapp.bangkok.go.th/arcgis/rest/services/GI_Platform/BMAGI_Planing/MapServer/1. Fields: LUP_ZONE, LUP_FAR, LUP_OSR, LAW_URL. Coordinates are EPSG:32647; request `outSR=4326` for WGS84.

## Zone ย.10 (brown, high-density residential), ข้อ 17 (H)
| Rule | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| FAR | 8 : 1 | ข้อ 17, https://drive.google.com/file/d/18fi25DtOw0jSB4JhfAClQVLF3kRzA9eP/view |
| OSR (open space ÷ total floor area) | ≥ 4% | ข้อ 17 |
| Planted, permeable open space | ≥ 50% of the open space | ข้อ 17 |
| Condo (อาคารอยู่อาศัยรวม) size or road conditions | none | ข้อ 17 prohibited-use list |
| FAR bonus | up to +20%; extra floor area ≤ 5× the public open space provided | ข้อ 53 |

| Rule | Value | Clause | Conf. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Open space, residential building | ≥ 30% of the largest floor area | MR 55 ข้อ 33(1) | H |
| What counts as open space | no roof over it; includes pools and outdoor parking; structures ≤ 1.20 m high count | MR 55 ข้อ 1 | H |
| Road setback, road < 6 m | ≥ 3 m from road centreline | MR 55 ข้อ 41 | H |
| Road setback, building > 2 storeys or > 8 m, road < 10 m | ≥ 6 m from road centreline | MR 55 ข้อ 41(1) | H |
| Road setback, road 10–20 m | ≥ 1/10 of road width from road boundary | MR 55 ข้อ 41(2) | H |
| Road setback, road > 20 m | ≥ 2 m from road boundary | MR 55 ข้อ 41(3) | H |
| Height plane | height at any point ≤ 2 × horizontal distance to the far boundary of the nearest public road | MR 55 ข้อ 44 | H |
| Height measured | from road or ground level to the highest point (for ข้อ 44) | MR 55 ข้อ 44 ¶2 | H |
| Two roads or a corner plot | use the wider road (conditions: ≤ 60 m apart / frontage ≤ 60 m) | MR 55 ข้อ 45, 46 | H |
| Window or balcony wall to boundary | ≥ 2 m if building ≤ 9 m; ≥ 3 m if 9–23 m | MR 55 ข้อ 50 | H |
| Spacing between buildings on one plot | ≤ 9 m: 4 m; 9–23 m: 6 m (amended by MR 61) | MR 55 ข้อ 48 | M |
| High-rise | height ≥ 23 m (ground to roof deck) | MR 33 ข้อ 1 | H |
| Extra-large building | ≥ 10,000 m² total floor area | MR 33 ข้อ 1 | H |
| Road and frontage for high-rise / extra-large | plot side ≥ 12 m long on a public road ≥ 10 m wide (≥ 18 m road if > 30,000 m²) | MR 33 ข้อ 2 (amended by MR 50) | H |
| Fire access | ≥ 6 m wide uncovered fire-truck road all round the building; may lie in the road setback | MR 33 ข้อ 3 | H |
| FAR ceiling, high-rise | ≤ 10 : 1 | MR 33 ข้อ 5 | H |
| Clear space all round, building > 15 m | ≥ 2 m | Bangkok Building Control Ordinance 2544 ข้อ 55 | H (secondary text) |
| Large building | > 2,000 m², or ≥ 15 m high and > 1,000 m² | Ordinance 2544 ข้อ 5(101) | H |
| Road width | full right-of-way width (ข้อ 5(4)); must hold along its whole length to a qualifying road (Supreme Admin. Court อ.588/2557) | — | H |
| Parking, condo in Bangkok | the larger of 1 space per unit ≥ 60 m² and 1 space per 120 m² of floor area | MR 7 + Ordinance 2544 | M |
| Parking space size | 2.40 × 5.00 m | MR 41 | M |
| EIA | condo ≥ 80 units or ≥ 4,000 m² | MNRE notification | M |

3	export type Pt = [number, number]
4	export type Poly = Pt[]

6	export const signedArea = (p: Poly) =>
7	  p.reduce((s, [x1, y1], i) => {
8	    const [x2, y2] = p[(i + 1) % p.length]
9	    return s + x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
10	  }, 0) / 2
11	
12	export const area = (p: Poly) => Math.abs(signedArea(p))
13	
14	export const ccw = (p: Poly): Poly => (signedArea(p) < 0 ? [...p].reverse() : p)
15	
16	export const edgeLengths = (p: Poly) =>
17	  p.map(([x1, y1], i) => {
18	    const [x2, y2] = p[(i + 1) % p.length]
19	    return Math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
20	  })
21	
22	export const centroid = (p: Poly): Pt => {
23	  const a = signedArea(p)
24	  let cx = 0, cy = 0
25	  p.forEach(([x1, y1], i) => {
26	    const [x2, y2] = p[(i + 1) % p.length]
27	    const f = x1 * y2 - x2 * y1
28	    cx += (x1 + x2) * f
29	    cy += (y1 + y2) * f
30	  })
31	  return [cx / (6 * a), cy / (6 * a)]
32	}
33	
34	const q = (v: number) => Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6
35	const qp = (p: Poly): Poly => p.map(([x, y]) => [q(x), q(y)])
36	
37	const capsule = ([ax, ay]: Pt, [bx, by]: Pt, r: number, seg = 12): Pt[] => {
38	  const t = Math.atan2(by - ay, bx - ax)
39	  const arc = (cx: number, cy: number, from: number) =>
40	    Array.from({ length: seg + 1 }, (_, i): Pt => {
41	      const a = from + (Math.PI * i) / seg
42	      return [q(cx + r * Math.cos(a)), q(cy + r * Math.sin(a))]
43	    })
44	  return [...arc(bx, by, t - Math.PI / 2), ...arc(ax, ay, t + Math.PI / 2)]
45	}
46	
47	const largest = (mp: pc.MultiPolygon): Poly =>
48	  mp.reduce<Poly>((best, poly) => {
49	    const ring = poly[0].slice(0, -1) as Poly
50	    return area(ring) > area(best) ? ring : best
51	  }, [])

53	/** Region at least setbacks[i] from edge i (edge i runs p[i] → p[i+1]). Concave-safe. */

55	  const p = ccw(plot)
56	  const flip = p !== plot
57	  const sb = flip ? p.map((_, i) => setbacks[(p.length - 2 - i + p.length) % p.length]) : setbacks

27	  const m = Math.max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) * 0.12 + 1
28	  const vb = [x0 - m, y0 - m, x1 - x0 + 2 * m, y1 - y0 + 2 * m]

2	import { edgeLengths, signedArea, type Poly, type Pt } from '../lib/geometry'
3	
4	export interface Underlay { url: string; width: number; height: number; mPerPx: number }
5	
6	interface Props {
7	  plot: Poly
8	  buildable: Poly
9	  footprint: Poly
10	  setbacks: number[]
11	  selectedEdge: number | null
12	  onEdge: (i: number) => void
13	  tracing: Pt[] | null
14	  onTrace: (p: Pt) => void
15	  underlay: Underlay | null
16	}
17	
18	const path = (p: Poly) => (p.length ? `M${p.map(([x, y]) => `${x},${-y}`).join('L')}Z` : '')
19	
20	export default function PlanView({ plot, buildable, footprint, setbacks, selectedEdge, onEdge, tracing, onTrace, underlay }: Props) {
21	  const pts = [...plot, ...(tracing ?? [])]
22	  const uw = underlay ? underlay.width * underlay.mPerPx : 0
23	  const uh = underlay ? underlay.height * underlay.mPerPx : 0
24	  const xs = [...pts.map(p => p[0]), ...(underlay ? [0, uw] : [])]
25	  const ys = [...pts.map(p => -p[1]), ...(underlay ? [-uh, 0] : [])]
26	  const [x0, x1, y0, y1] = [Math.min(...xs), Math.max(...xs), Math.min(...ys), Math.max(...ys)]
27	  const m = Math.max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0) * 0.12 + 1
28	  const vb = [x0 - m, y0 - m, x1 - x0 + 2 * m, y1 - y0 + 2 * m]
29	  const fs = vb[2] / 40
30	  const lens = edgeLengths(plot)
31	  const ccwPlot = signedArea(plot) > 0
32	
33	  const click = (e: MouseEvent<SVGSVGElement>) => {
34	    if (!tracing) return
35	    const svg = e.currentTarget
36	    const pt = new DOMPoint(e.clientX, e.clientY).matrixTransform(svg.getScreenCTM()!.inverse())
37	    onTrace([Math.round(pt.x * 100) / 100, Math.round(-pt.y * 100) / 100])
38	  }
39	
40	  return (
41	    <svg viewBox={vb.join(' ')} onClick={click} className={tracing ? 'plan tracing' : 'plan'} role="img" aria-label="Site plan">
42	      {underlay && <image href={underlay.url} x={0} y={-uh} width={uw} height={uh} opacity={0.6} />}
43	      <path d={path(plot)} fill="#c9d8b6" stroke="#3b4a3a" strokeWidth={fs / 6} />
44	      <path d={path(buildable)} fill="none" stroke="#b45309" strokeWidth={fs / 8} strokeDasharray={`${fs / 2} ${fs / 3}`} />
45	      <path d={path(footprint)} fill="#2563eb" fillOpacity={0.35} stroke="#1d4ed8" strokeWidth={fs / 8} />
46	      {!tracing &&
47	        plot.map(([ax, ay], i) => {
48	          const [bx, by] = plot[(i + 1) % plot.length]
49	          const k = (fs * 0.9 * (ccwPlot ? 1 : -1)) / Math.hypot(bx - ax, by - ay)
50	          const [mx, my] = [(ax + bx) / 2 + (by - ay) * k, (ay + by) / 2 - (bx - ax) * k]
51	          return (
52	            <g key={i} onClick={() => onEdge(i)} className="edge">
53	              <line x1={ax} y1={-ay} x2={bx} y2={-by} stroke={selectedEdge === i ? '#dc2626' : 'transparent'} strokeWidth={fs / 2} />
54	              <text x={mx} y={-my} fontSize={fs} textAnchor="middle" dominantBaseline="middle">
55	                E{i + 1} · {lens[i].toFixed(1)} m · sb {setbacks[i] ?? 0}
56	              </text>
57	            </g>
58	          )
59	        })}
60	      {tracing && (
61	        <>
62	          <polyline points={tracing.map(([x, y]) => `${x},${-y}`).join(' ')} fill="none" stroke="#dc2626" strokeWidth={fs / 6} />
63	          {tracing.map(([x, y], i) => <circle key={i} cx={x} cy={-y} r={fs / 3} fill="#dc2626" />)}
64	        </>
65	      )}
66	      <g transform={`translate(${vb[0] + vb[2] - fs * 2},${vb[1] + fs * 2})`}>
67	        <path d={`M0,${-fs} L${fs / 2},${fs / 2} L0,0 L${-fs / 2},${fs / 2}Z`} fill="#111" />
68	        <text y={fs * 1.6} fontSize={fs} textAnchor="middle">N</text>
69	      </g>
70	    </svg>
71	  )

import sys, time
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

url = sys.argv[1]
out = sys.argv[2]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(args=["--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    for name, vp in (("desk", {"width": 1440, "height": 900}), ("phone", {"width": 390, "height": 844})):
        pg = b.new_page(viewport=vp, device_scale_factor=1)
        logs = []
        pg.on("console", lambda m: logs.append(f"{m.type}: {m.text}"))
        pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: logs.append(f"PAGEERROR: {e}"))
        t = time.time()
        pg.goto(url, wait_until="networkidle", timeout=90000)
        pg.wait_for_timeout(6000)
        pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\{name}.png", full_page=(name == "phone"))
        print(name, f"{time.time()-t:.1f}s")
        print(pg.inner_text(".right")[:900] if name == "desk" else "")
        for l in logs[:15]: print("  ", l[:300])
        pg.close()
    b.close()

import sys, time
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

url = sys.argv[1]
out = sys.argv[2]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(args=["--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    for name, vp in (("desk", {"width": 1440, "height": 900}), ("phone", {"width": 390, "height": 844})):
        pg = b.new_page(viewport=vp, device_scale_factor=1)
        logs = []
        pg.on("console", lambda m: logs.append(f"{m.type}: {m.text}"))
        pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: logs.append(f"PAGEERROR: {e}"))
        t = time.time()
        pg.goto(url, wait_until="load", timeout=90000)
        pg.wait_for_timeout(9000)
        pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\{name}.png", full_page=(name == "phone"))
        print(name, f"{time.time()-t:.1f}s")
        print(pg.inner_text(".right")[:900] if name == "desk" else "")
        for l in logs[:15]: print("  ", l[:300])
        pg.close()
    b.close()

input.content:
import sys, time
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
url, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
card = lambda pg: pg.inner_text(".cards").replace("\n", " | ")
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(args=["--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900})
    errs = []
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
    pg.on("console", lambda m: m.type == "error" and errs.append(m.text))
    pg.goto(url, wait_until="load")
    pg.wait_for_timeout(8000)
    print("START", card(pg))
    url0 = pg.url

    # drag a plot corner: find vertex screen position through the map
    pt = pg.evaluate("""() => { const c = document.querySelector('.maplibregl-canvas'); const r = c.getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.left, r.top, r.width, r.height] }""")
    # 1) road width 8
    inp = pg.locator("section:has(h2:text('2 · Road')) input[type=number]")
    inp.fill("8"); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("W=8  ", card(pg))
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\w8.png")
    inp.fill("12"); pg.wait_for_timeout(1000)
    # 2) hotel
    pg.get_by_role("button", name="Hotel").click(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("HOTEL", card(pg))
    pg.get_by_role("button", name="Condominium").click(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1000)
    # 3) toggle height plane off
    pg.locator(".rule:has-text('Height vs road') input").uncheck(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("PLANE OFF", card(pg))
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\planeoff.png")
    pg.locator(".rule:has-text('Height vs road') input").check(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1000)
    # 4) draw a new plot somewhere nearby (map centre area)
    x0, y0, w, h = pt
    pg.get_by_role("button", name="Draw new plot").click()
    pts = [(x0 + w * 0.70, y0 + h * 0.70), (x0 + w * 0.85, y0 + h * 0.68), (x0 + w * 0.88, y0 + h * 0.85), (x0 + w * 0.72, y0 + h * 0.88)]
    for (x, y) in pts:
        pg.mouse.click(x, y); pg.wait_for_timeout(250)
    pg.keyboard.press("Enter"); pg.wait_for_timeout(4000)
    print("NEWPLOT", pg.inner_text(".big"), "|", card(pg))
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\newplot.png")
    # 5) drag a vertex of the new plot
    pg.mouse.move(*pts[2]); pg.mouse.down()
    for k in range(12):
        pg.mouse.move(pts[2][0] + 6 * k, pts[2][1] + 3 * k); pg.wait_for_timeout(30)
    pg.mouse.up(); pg.wait_for_timeout(2000)
    print("DRAG", pg.inner_text(".big"), "|", card(pg))
    print("URL changed:", pg.url != url0)
    # 6) self-intersecting attempt: drag vertex 0 across
    pg.mouse.move(*pts[0]); pg.mouse.down(); pg.mouse.move(x0 + w * 0.95, y0 + h * 0.95, steps=8); pg.mouse.up(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("BANNER", pg.locator(".banner").all_inner_texts())
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\cross.png")
    print("ERRORS", errs[:8])
    b.close()

import sys, time
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
url, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(args=["--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900})
    errs = []
    pg.on("pageerror", lambda e: errs.append(str(e)))
    pg.goto(url, wait_until="load"); pg.wait_for_timeout(8000)
    vert = lambda i: pg.evaluate("""(i) => { const m = window.__map; const f = m.getSource('verts')._data; const c = (f.features || f.geojson?.features)[i].geometry.coordinates; const p = m.project(c); const r = m.getCanvas().getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.left + p.x, r.top + p.y] }""", i)
    big = lambda: pg.inner_text(".big")
    card = lambda: pg.inner_text(".card.on").replace("\n", " | ")
    print("before", big(), "|", card())
    x, y = vert(2)
    pg.mouse.move(x, y); pg.mouse.down()
    t = time.time()
    for k in range(20):
        pg.mouse.move(x + 3 * k, y - 2 * k); pg.wait_for_timeout(16)
    mid = big()
    pg.mouse.up(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print(f"during {mid} ({(time.time()-t)*1000:.0f} ms for 20 moves)")
    print("after ", big(), "|", card())
    # insert via midpoint, then delete via right-click
    pg.evaluate("window.__map.jumpTo({})")
    mx = pg.evaluate("""() => { const m = window.__map; const f = m.getSource('mids')._data; const c = (f.features || f.geojson?.features)[0].geometry.coordinates; const p = m.project(c); const r = m.getCanvas().getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.left + p.x, r.top + p.y] }""")
    pg.mouse.click(*mx); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("insert", big())
    x, y = vert(1)
    pg.mouse.click(x, y, button="right"); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("delete", big())
    # toggle road edge by clicking edge 2 midpoint area (the mid handle sits there, so click near it on the edge)
    # cross edges: drag vertex 0 far beyond vertex 3
    x0, y0 = vert(0); x3, y3 = vert(3)
    pg.mouse.move(x0, y0); pg.mouse.down(); pg.mouse.move(x3 + (x3 - x0) * 0.8, y3 + (y3 - y0) * 0.8, steps=10); pg.mouse.up(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("cross banner", pg.locator(".banner").all_inner_texts())
    pg.screenshot(path=f"{out}\\cross.png")
    print("ERRORS", errs[:5])
    b.close()

import sys
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
url = sys.argv[1]
with sync_playwright() as p:
    b = p.chromium.launch(args=["--use-gl=angle", "--use-angle=swiftshader", "--enable-unsafe-swiftshader"])
    pg = b.new_page(viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900})
    pg.goto(url, wait_until="load"); pg.wait_for_timeout(8000)
    # pure map render cost: rotate camera for 2 s with nothing else changing
    fps = pg.evaluate("""() => new Promise(res => { const m = window.__map; let n = 0; const t0 = performance.now();
      const step = () => { m.setBearing(m.getBearing() + 1); n++; if (performance.now() - t0 < 2000) requestAnimationFrame(step); else res(n / ((performance.now() - t0) / 1000)) };
      requestAnimationFrame(step) })""")
    print(f"map-only frames/s (software GL): {fps:.1f}")
    # long tasks during a drag
    pg.evaluate("""() => { window.__lt = []; new PerformanceObserver(l => l.getEntries().forEach(e => window.__lt.push(Math.round(e.duration)))).observe({ type: 'longtask', buffered: false }) }""")
    vert = pg.evaluate("""() => { const m = window.__map; const f = m.getSource('verts')._data; const c = (f.features || f.geojson?.features)[2].geometry.coordinates; const p = m.project(c); const r = m.getCanvas().getBoundingClientRect(); return [r.left + p.x, r.top + p.y] }""")
    x, y = vert
    pg.mouse.move(x, y); pg.mouse.down()
    for k in range(10):
        pg.mouse.move(x + 3 * k, y - 2 * k)
    pg.mouse.up(); pg.wait_for_timeout(1500)
    print("long tasks during drag (ms):", pg.evaluate("window.__lt"))
    b.close()

content.text:
The first working version is live at **https://siliconbricks-assignment.vercel.app**. It opens with a sample plot preloaded.

**What it does**
- **Plot:** a 2,776 m², six-corner plot on Soi Sukhumvit 39, which the official BMA zoning layer places in zone ย.10. You can drag corners, click a mid-point to add one, right-click to remove one, or draw a new plot. Edges that face a road are found automatically, and clicking an edge toggles it.
- **Rules:** each rule shows its clause, a link to its source, and a label: sourced, secondary source, interpretation or assumption. Each rule can be switched off to show how it shapes the allowed space. The rules are:
  - FAR and OSR from the 2013 Bangkok Comprehensive Plan
  - road setback, height limited by road width, and open space from Ministerial Regulation 55
  - high-rise road access and fire access from Ministerial Regulation 33
  - parking requirement
  - when an environmental impact assessment is triggered
- **Allowed space:** it follows the real plot outline and steps back floor by floor as the height-vs-road rule bites.
- **Designs:** three concept designs, each with a pass/fail checklist and a floor-by-floor area statement whose floor areas add up to the total (a unit test checks this).
- **Real site:** 4,559 real buildings and the surrounding roads from OpenStreetMap in 3D. Only 7% of those buildings have a mapped height; the rest are estimated, drawn lighter and labelled as estimates. Plots outside the bundled area load buildings live from OpenStreetMap and look up the zone live from the BMA layer.
- **Live updates:** the calculation runs in a background thread, so dragging a corner no longer blocks the page.

**Checks I ran**
- 15 unit tests pass, along with type-check and build.
- In a real browser on the live site:
  - At a 12 m road width the tower is 28 floors, 87.5 m, FAR 8.00, with every check passing.
  - At 8 m the tool switches to low-rise designs under 10,000 m², and the tower fails its road-access check.
  - Switching to hotel updated everything.
  - Turning off the height-vs-road rule makes the towers fail that check.
  - Drawing a new plot, dragging, adding and removing corners, and the warning when edges cross all work.
  - There were no console errors.
- Desktop and phone layouts are checked. In headless testing the 3D view renders at only about 16 frames/s, but that is the test machine's software graphics; I haven't measured it on a real laptop yet.

**Changes from the plan**
- I added hotel and office as building types, because the brief says changing the building type should update everything. Only the condo parking rule is sourced; hotel and office parking use an assumed rate.
- Two calls are interpretations rather than direct readings of the law, both labelled as such in the tool and in [DECISIONS.md](DECISIONS.md):
  - the 6 m side and rear setback for high-rises, read from the fire-access rule
  - hotels being held to 10% open space instead of the residential 30%

**Please commit and push now.** This is the first working increment. Suggested message: `Bangkok ย.10 plot feasibility: rules, stepped envelope, 3 designs, OSM context, live map`.

**Next:** I'll try to break it with odd plot shapes and very narrow lanes, test live loading outside the bundled area, explain on each design why it stops short of the maximum FAR, then write the README and polish. That's on track for a first submission by Sat 21 Nov, 18:00 IST.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
